title: Understanding the Residual Vector
text: The residual vector e is defined as the difference between the observed values Y and the predicted values \(\hat{Y}\). This vector represents the error or deviation of the observed data from the model's predictions.

title: Orthogonality in OLS
text: In the context of Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), the residual vector e is orthogonal to the columns of the design matrix X. This means that the dot product of e with any column of X is zero.

title: Implications of Orthogonality
text: The orthogonality condition implies that the residuals do not provide any additional information that could improve the model's fit. This is a key property of the OLS estimator.

title: Checking Orthogonality
text: To verify the orthogonality, calculate the dot product of the residual vector e with each column of the design matrix X. If the dot product is zero, the vectors are orthogonal.
